transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
A federal judge in Washington, D.C. is siding with three media outlets U.S. District Judge
Timothy Kelly is ordering the Trump administration to restore White House access for journalists
from CNN, MS Now and Politico, saying Trump's ban on their reporters is likely unconstitutional.
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is scolding open AI over the security breach
of a government website and says an investigation will examine whether open AI should be criminally
charged.
A forensic investigation aided by the Australian Signals Directorate is now underway to ascertain
more information including what other government systems were affected.
Albanese made the breach public after he said he spoke by phone with open AI chief Sam Altman
to express what he said is Australia's extreme concern.
Both are in New York City for the U.N. General Assembly.
Open AI notified Australia of the breach of a health department website earlier this month
by email to a generic government address.
The breach happened back in July.
The Australian government says no personal information was accessed.
U.S. and China have agreed to extend by two months a trade war that was due to expire,
a trade war truce that was due to expire.
The announcement Wednesday came as China's president Xi Jinping arrived in the U.S. NPR's
Emily Fang reports that President Trump greeted the Chinese leader on the tarmac at Joint
Base Andrews.
A welcoming delegation unfurled a 100-foot-long red carpet for Xi and his wife.
They were met by the president and the first lady, a gesture seen in China as acknowledging
the country is equal to the U.S.
The last time a U.S. president received a head of state on the tarmac at Joint Base
Andrews was 1962.
Xi and Trump will have a day of meetings spanning trade to technology and the war in Iran, and
a state news agency praised the upcoming meeting, saying they can steer the relationship towards
a more stable one.
But under the surface, Chinese and American officials say deep distrust and disagreement
remain on issues ranging from Taiwan to artificial intelligence.
Emily Fang, NPR News, the White House.
NPR's Kat Lonstorff reports on growing concern that President Trump could deploy National
Guard troops around polling locations in November.
A growing number of Democratic lawmakers, retired military leaders, and civil society
organizations are seeking assurance from the Trump administration that the military will
not be deployed to polling places, while also preparing for such a move to occur.
Having federal troops or armed agents near the polls is clearly barred by federal law.
But President Trump and several other key officials have recently sidestepped direct
lines of questioning around the issue.
And Trump has already shown a willingness to deploy the military domestically, particularly
the National Guard.
Meanwhile, voting officials across the country say they plan on administering the midterms
as usual and are assuring voters there are plans in place if federal agents do show up
to the polls.
Kat Lonstorff, NPR News.
This is NPR.
Police in Mississippi have made a second arrest in the death of a black woman found hanging
from a tree and have issued an arrest warrant for a third suspect.
Both suspects in custody are black, and the first man arrested was denied bond during a
court hearing Wednesday.
Twenty-nine-year-old Tayshia Porgin's body was found behind an abandoned home last month.
Harvey Weinstein's New York sex crimes case came to a close Wednesday morning when the
former movie "Mogul" was sentenced to 15 years in prison, impures Chloe Weiner reports.
Harvey Weinstein was first convicted of sex crimes in New York in 2020, and sentenced
to 23 years in prison.
But that was thrown out.
Prosecutors have since brought him back to court multiple times.
Last year Weinstein was found guilty of sexually assaulting Miriam Haley in 2006 when she
was a production assistant.
The 15-year sentence is from that conviction.
Weinstein was found not guilty on another charge, and two separate juries in New York
have been unable to reach a verdict on a charge of rape.
He was, however, convicted of rape in California in 2022.
He was sentenced to 16 years, but a court ruled earlier this year that he will need to
be re-sentenced.
Weinstein is now 74 years old and has numerous health problems.
He is pleaded not guilty to all charges.
Chloe Weiner, NPR News, New York.
An amateur archaeologist has discovered a hoard of Roman silver coins in western Germany.
The coins were found in a field near Veseling, south of Cologne.
The local archaeologist's office confirmed this week that it's the largest coin treasure
from the time of Roman Emperor Hadrian found in Germany.
The exact worth remains unclear.
I'm Charles Snyder, NPR News.
